findings.source_issue: The source asks for a smooth map of a line onto a plane and then calls Peano's space-filling curve just such an example. Peano's compact-interval-to-square map is continuous, not smooth; a continuously differentiable curve on a compact interval is Lipschitz and its planar image has area zero.
findings.minimal_treatment: Describe the Peano construction as a continuous map from a line segment onto a square, and disclose the smoothness/continuity distinction.
